newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish insurers' bond holdings rose further in H1.
newsitem.headline: Finnish insurers' bond holdings rose further in H1.

text.p: Finnish insurers' investments in government bonds rose by 11 billion markka to 73.6 billion in the first half of the year, the Federation of Finnish Insurance Companies said in a statement on Thursday.

At end-June, insurers had allocated 34.9 percent of their 211.0 billion markka total portfolios in government bonds, it said. At end-1995, government bonds accounted for 32.4 percent of a total insurance sector investment stock of 184.3 billion.
In 1995, Finnish insurers increased their holdings in government bonds by 70 percent.
Shares also became more popular in the first half of 1996, accounting for 13.7 percent of the investment stock at end-June compared to 11.0 percent at end-1995.
Pension insurers' lending back to corporations, on the other hand, fell further to account for 18.7 percent of all investments compared to 23.1 percent at the turn of the year, the federation said.
Other bonds' portion of insurers' investments fell to 8.6 percent from 10.7 percent, and real estate's slice fell to 14.8 percent from 16.2 percent.
